Bridge to the Derivative

When evaluating the derivative $f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}$, direct substitution of $h = 0$ always yields the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}$! As shown by the dashed curves above, both the numerator $N(h)$ and denominator $D(h)$ collapse to zero simultaneously. The limit resolves this $\frac{0}{0}$ hole into a well-defined finite number: the exact instantaneous tangent slope.
